vulnerability.category_l2: Client-side denial of service: presence keys named after Object.prototype members make the presence client read .metas off a built-in and throw

critical_operation.description: Presence.syncState/4 clones the current state into a plain object (line 69) and then uses bare bracket lookups plus truthiness tests on attacker-influenced presence keys: line 74 tests !newState[key] and line 79 reads currentPresence = state[key]. A key named after an Object.prototype member (__proto__, constructor, hasOwnProperty, toString, ...) resolves through the prototype chain to a built-in value instead of undefined, so line 80 treats it as an existing presence and line 82 calls currentPresence.metas.map(...), throwing an uncaught TypeError because the built-in has no metas array. The same pattern exists in syncDiff/4 at lines 115-120. The exception propagates out of the channel presence_state/presence_diff handler (lines 21-32 and 34-43), so the local state is not updated and onSync() never runs, leaving every viewer of the topic with a presence client that no longer processes updates. The 1.6 fix 89a1c4be creates the state with Object.create(null), converts inputs through toNullProtoObj/1, and adds the __proto__/constructor/hasOwnProperty regression tests (CWE-754).

entry_point.description: A user with ordinary channel access joins a presence channel using a presence key that is an Object.prototype member name; the server then sends presence_state or presence_diff over the channel, and the client hands the decoded object to Presence.syncState/syncDiff.

source_crosscheck.notes: CVE, NVD and OSV agree on CWE-754, the affected ranges and the 1.6.17 fix. Severity is published in two metric versions: CVSS 4.0 6.3 Medium (CNA, OSV, NVD Secondary; AT:P and VA:L) and CVSS 3.1 7.5 High (NVD Primary; A:H). The bands differ because the metric versions differ; no source disagrees within the same version. OSV's fixed-commit list includes 2270aaf, which local history shows is the 2016 commit that introduced the Presence client, an upstream metadata defect; the real branch fixes 7f7b971c/89a1c4be/b90b2252/beffc4da map to 1.5.15/1.6.17/1.7.24/1.8.9 by ancestry. The same file ships in npm phoenix (root package.json files list assets/js/phoenix/*) as well as the hex package.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Presence.syncState/syncDiff at v1.6.13 and confirm that bare bracket lookups on plain objects resolve Object.prototype members for keys such as __proto__ or constructor and that .metas.map then throws.
An independent reviewer must confirm 89a1c4be is the 1.6-branch fix, not an ancestor of 1.6.13/1.6.16 and contained in 1.6.17.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected ranges, the CVSS 4.0 / 3.1 records, and whether the client-side impact claim is supported.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

independent_verdict.outcome: not promoted: the reviewer set severity_consistent=false because NVD's primary CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH record disagrees with the CNA/OSV/GHSA CVSS 4.0 6.3 MEDIUM record

independent_corrections_accepted: The reviewer verified a wider line range (74-130) covering both syncState and syncDiff; the dossier keeps 68-82 as the critical operation window.
The snapshot's built artifacts priv/static/phoenix.js, phoenix.cjs.js and phoenix.mjs also contain the vulnerable presence code; the dossier now notes the npm bundle surface.

GHSA-63mc-hw7g-86rr says the fix adds Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call gating, but the actual fix uses Object.create(null) and toNullProtoObj/1; the GHSA wording is imprecise and is recorded as an upstream defect.
The advisory omits the equivalent main-branch fix e84b8f6a (ancestor of main e5880ef7), so the CNA git range cannot mark current main unaffected.
The OSV-EEF GitHub affected-version enumeration omits several tags inside the declared ranges (for example v1.5.14, v1.6.8/v1.6.9, v1.7.17/v1.7.21); the ranges themselves are still correct.
The impact precondition is narrower than GHSA's 'any authenticated channel participant': the application must derive the presence key from untrusted client input.
Severity: NVD primary CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH versus CNA/OSV/GHSA CVSS 4.0 6.3 MEDIUM; the reviewer judged the published records inconsistent and the promotion gate therefore fails on severity_consistent.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.

The independent reviewer set severity_consistent=false (NVD CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH vs CNA/OSV/GHSA CVSS 4.0 6.3 MEDIUM); the vulnerability was not promoted and stays pending a severity-convention decision.
No browser, JavaScript runtime, WebSocket client or channel server was executed; the crash path is established statically from the prototype-chain lookup and the .metas.map call.

Impact requires the attacker to control a presence key (applications commonly use a client-supplied username or id) and affects viewers of that presence topic; it is client-side denial of service, not server compromise.
Only the 1.6 branch was diffed; the 1.5.15, 1.7.24 and 1.8.9 fixed trees were not inspected.
OSV lists the introducing commit 2270aaf as fixed; that is an upstream metadata defect, and the branch fixes are mapped by local ancestry instead.
The npm package was not downloaded; its affectedness is taken from the CNA and from the repository's root package.json files list, not from an npm tarball inspection.
open_questions: Whether every server-side presence implementation allows a client-chosen key literally named __proto__ was not audited; the advisory states that presence keys can be attacker-controlled, and this dossier relies on that statement.
